subject: Private deployment partitioning narrative + SIG-lite walkthrough for Meridian Health
messages:
From: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@meridianhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@meridianhealth.com, security@meridianhealth.com
Date: 2027-03-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment: request for partitioning narrative + SIG-lite mapping

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of Meridian Health's security review for Private deployment we need a short narrative (1-2 pages) describing how Redwood partitions customer workloads in a private/VPC deployment, plus a SIG-lite mapping that calls out the specific SIG questions we care about (network isolation, egress controls, control plane separation).

Specific asks:
- One-page network partitioning narrative that we can attach to our SOC 2 binder (call out VPC routing, peering, and any airgap/airlock options).
- A SIG-lite spreadsheet that maps your answers to SIG v2 questions we flagged (network enclave, control-plane isolation, evidence pointers).
- Any compact diagrams you can share showing the Private control plane vs data plane paths and egress enforcement.

Target timeline: we need a packet to to hand to our auditors by 2027-03-22. Can you confirm?

Appreciate it — alex

--
Alex Jordan
Director, IT Risk & Vendor Security
Meridian Health

1) Laura will assemble a one-page narrative and cover note for auditors.
2) Dev will produce a succinct topology diagram and an annotated packet-trace showing egress enforcement flows.
3) I'll own the SIG-lite spreadsheet and map answers to the questions you flagged; we will include evidence pointers (Drive links + attachment stubs).

- Do you need the diagram to show VPC-peering only, or also the on-prem private-connect (Meridian DX circuits) we demoed?
- For KMS boundary language: do auditors require KMS/HSM attestation or is a KMS control statement sufficient for now?

Looping in Dev and Laura to start compiling.

From: dev.patel@redwood.com <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-17T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: request for partitioning narrative + SIG-lite mapping

Karthik / Laura — drafting the tech appendix now. Initial notes (for inclusion in the one-page narrative and the diagram):

1) Deployment modes captured: 
- Private (customer VPC with Redwood Private agents in their VPC / on-prem rack).
- Private with Dedicated GPU pools (reserved capacity nodes isolated to customer-run subnets).

2) Partitioning model (short):
- Control plane: managed by Redwood but logically isolated; control-plane APIs run in a separate account/namespace and use mutual TLS + per-customer API creds. No control-plane egress to customer subnets.
- Data plane: runs inside customer VPC (or on-prem). Data plane hosts (in dedicated subnets) hold model runtime and metadata. Network ACLs + security groups block lateral management-plane access.

3) Egress enforcement and eBPF hooks:
- All outbound flows from model runtime pass through a configurable egress-proxy (sidecar or gateway), where we enforce destination allowlists. We capture the final flow with eBPF-based flow-tap for audit (stubs attached).
- For customers requiring stronger isolation we offer an airlock pattern: explicit NAT-only egress, with egress auditing bundles provided as evidence.

4) Peering & private-connect:
- Supported: VPC-peering, Private-Peering (Transit Gateway), and IPsec DX circuits. Peering is restricted to a small set of service IPs; control plane uses separate endpoints and never traverses customer service subnets.

5) Key management boundary:
- Customer-managed KMS supported; Redwood can integrate with customer KMS (KMIP / Cloud KMS). For SOC 2 purposes we provide a control narrative and examples of KMS key usage logs. HSM attestation available as an add-on.

Attachments I'm preparing:
- meridian_network_sketch_v1.pdf (diagram annotated with subnets and peering lanes)
- packet-trace-annotated.png (example egress flow vs allowed destinations)
- private-deploy-egress-playbook.md (short runbook for auditor reference)

I'll ping when drafts are ready for Laura to assemble.

--
Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-17T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: request for partitioning narrative + SIG-lite mapping

Alex — attaching the packet for Meridian (first pass). See attachments below. Short summary:

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Redwood Private deploys a split-control architecture where the Redwood control plane (management APIs, model catalog, job scheduler) is logically separated from customer data plane runtime. Customers receive network-level partitioning through dedicated subnets, explicit peering controls (Transit Gateway or DX), and configurable egress proxies. For customers requiring additional assurance we provide an airlock pattern and KMS-integration with customer-managed keys.

Key artifacts attached: 
- meridian_network_sketch_v1.pdf — annotated topology showing control plane endpoints, transit peering lanes, egress proxy, and audit taps.
- sig_response_matrix.xlsx — compact SIG-lite mapping (question id, short answer, evidence pointer).
- private-deploy-egress-playbook.md — runbook describing how egress is enforced and how auditors can validate flows.
- packet-trace-annotated.png — example captured flow showing DNS resolution, egress-proxy, and allowed destination handshake.

Requested clarifications we noted from your original list: 
- Diagrams include both VPC-peering and an optional DX circuit lane (we labeled both in the PDF).
- KMS: we included language for customer-managed KMS and an HSM add-on statement. If auditors need HSM certs we can provide the attestation addendum (separate doc).

Next steps / ask of Meridian: 
1) Please confirm whether you want the DX circuit lane drawn to include your on-prem firewall (yes/no).
2) Confirm auditors are okay with SIG-lite answers and the Drive links; if they ask for raw logs we will prepare a timeboxed sample export.
3) If you want a live walkthrough we can schedule a 45-minute session next week.

If that timeline works we will finalize the SIG spreadsheet and send a DocuSign-ready evidence index for your procurement team.

Best,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Laura / team — thanks, this looks good as a first pass. A couple of quick items from the auditor: 
- Please add an explicit column in the SIG-lite mapping that references SOC 2 common criteria (e.g., CC6.1/CC6.2) where the network control ties to a control objective.
- For the packet-trace image can you include a brief note that identifies the eBPF tap point (node-level or host-side) and retention window for captured metadata.

We would like the live walkthrough — can you do 2027-03-23 at 10:00am PT? Procurement will want the DocuSign evidence index once the SIG-lite is finalized.

If you can update the matrix with the SOC 2 crosswalk and a 1-line eBPF retention note before the walkthrough, that should keep auditors happy.

Thanks — Alex
